items.description: Most or all of your 6 gear pieces (mask, chest, backpack, gloves, holster, kneepads) have Red set as their core attribute — maximizes weapon damage at the cost of survivability and skill power.
Most pieces are set to the Blue core — maximizes Total Armor and survivability, the default for tanks and frontline builds.
Most pieces are set to the Yellow core — maximizes Skill Tier and skill power, the default for skill and support builds.
Roughly half your pieces are Red, half Blue — a damage/survivability hybrid used by most Heroic-farming builds.
Split between weapon damage and skill power — used by hybrid weapon-skill loadouts like Capacitor builds, where your gun scales off Skill Tier.
Split between skill power and survivability — the standard split for healer and support builds that need to stay alive while channeling skills.
An explicit piece count instead of a general 'mix' — here, 3 of your 6 pieces are on Blue core and the rest on Red, used when a build needs a guaranteed survivability floor.
An even split, two pieces on each core — used by cross-core sets like Core Strength that convert a share of your off-core bonuses back to you.
A deployable riot shield you carry that blocks incoming fire from the front.
The mobile ballistic shield skill — you carry it and can fire your weapon around or over it while it blocks damage.
Shield variants (mod/skin choices) tuned toward stacking bonus damage the longer it's up, or toward holding aggro and soaking damage.
A deployable support drone that hovers near you or an ally and applies an ongoing effect.
Automatically revives and heals downed allies (or yourself) who are within its range.
Pulses armor repair to you and nearby allies over time — the core skill of most healer builds.
Launches a swarm of small attack drones at nearby enemies instead of healing.
A radar-style burst that reveals and debuffs enemies in range, including through walls.
Marks enemies through walls and grants bonus critical hit chance against marked targets.
A sonic burst that disorients and damages nearby enemies instead of just revealing them.
Disables enemy skills, cameras and turrets caught in its blast radius — the go-to answer to enemy skill spam in PvP.
A deployable, stationary gun that tracks and fires at enemies on its own.
A mounted machine gun turret with strong sustained single-target damage.
A turret variant that sprays fire in an arc instead of firing bullets — built for status/burn builds.
A flying combat drone that either attacks on its own or protects you.
Aggressively chases down and attacks the nearest enemy without your input.
Hovers near you or an ally and intercepts incoming damage.
A grenade launcher that fires chemical rounds instead of explosives.
Coats an area in a cloud that repairs the armor of anyone standing in it.
Fires an expanding foam that traps and immobilizes enemies caught in it — the core of every crowd-control build.
Fires an incendiary round that ignites enemies and the ground beneath them.
A standalone gadget that throws a holographic decoy to distract enemies and pull their aggro.
A small utility drone that seeks out a target enemy and detonates or applies an effect on arrival.
One of the three colors (Red, Blue, Yellow) that a gear piece's largest attribute slot is locked to — see the Foundations section above.
A 0–6 scale built almost entirely from Yellow-core attributes; each tier unlocks a stronger tier of skill mods, so most skill builds chase Skill Tier 6 before anything else.
Your chance to land a critical hit, and how much bonus damage that critical hit does when it lands.
Reduces incoming damage from environmental and status sources — gas, fire, radiation and similar hazards.
Reduces the duration or effect of enemy disabling skills, like being pulsed, jammed or disrupted.

items.term: Armor on Kill / Health on Kill
items.description: Instantly restores a chunk of armor or health whenever you get a kill — a common sustain tool for aggressive close-range builds.
The hardest standard mission difficulty below Legendary — needs a reasonably optimized build to clear comfortably.
The top mission difficulty, tuned around a full 4-person group running near-max gear.
The current endgame activity and the main source of most current-season exotic weapons and armor.
A tower-climb endgame mode with escalating floors and stacking modifiers.

The hybrid PvE/PvP zone where other real players can attack you and steal your loot. Since Red Horizon it's split into normalized Toxic DZ (permanent, solo-safe) and full-power Blackout DZ (rotates weekly, uncapped stats) — see the PvP Builds section.
The dedicated, structured competitive PvP mode.
A small-group, high-difficulty scripted encounter — shorter and smaller than a raid, but built the same way.
The largest scripted endgame encounter, built for 8 players running defined roles like tank, healer and DPS.
An optional modifier you can toggle on a mission for bonus rewards in exchange for extra difficulty.
The older power-level number stamped on a piece of gear, capped at 515 — see the Recalibration & Optimization Workflow section.
The endgame progression system that takes over once you've hit the Gear Score cap, unlocking perks instead of raw power.
A per-item mastery track (caps at 30) that unlocks extra perks on that specific piece and is required before it can be converted to Prototype.
The currency spent at the Protolab to convert an eligible piece of gear into Prototype quality.
The highest gear quality tier — raises a piece's attribute ceiling and adds a bonus Augment slot, but locks it out of further Recalibration or Optimization.
A bonus perk (Quantum, Echo, Atomize or Amalgam) that only appears on Prototype-converted gear.
A talent effect that gets stronger the longer a condition keeps being met — like Striker's Gamble growing while you fire without reloading — usually up to a cap.
How much of an actual fight a talent's bonus is active for. A talent that's amazing on paper but hard to keep active has poor uptime.
Community slang for a talent effect triggering — 'it procs when you land a headshot' means the effect fires on headshot hits.
A status effect (like Trap, Blind or Disorient) that 'primes' a target, which a separate skill or weapon talent can then 'detonate' for bonus damage.
An enemy currently revealed or tagged by a Pulse skill — several talents (like Flatline) only trigger against pulsed targets.
An enemy tagged by a skill or talent, such as Hostile Negotiations, for bonus or shared damage.
A damage-over-time or debuff effect applied to an enemy — Bleed, Burn, Blind, Disorient and Trap are the main ones.
